newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile seizes dead Mexican drug baron's cars.
newsitem.headline: Chile seizes dead Mexican drug baron's cars.

text.p: Chilean officials said on Wednesday they have seized 11 luxury cars and raided plush mansions rented in Santiago by Mexican drug lord Amado Carrillo Fuentes who died after plastic surgery last month.
Chilean and Mexican anti-narcotics police kept close tabs on the movements of Carrillo, who was in the country from May until July 3, Deputy Interior Minister Belisario Velasco said.
"It's clear that Carrillo Fuentes, who died in strange circumstances on July 4, was in Chile, made contacts ... people came who were working for his cartel," Velasco told reporters.
A Mexican television program reported on Tuesday that Carrillo, who had been a fugitive from justice for years, was planning to move his drug smuggling cartel to Chile.
Chilean courts, using information from Mexico, ordered police to seize the Mercedes Benz cars and search houses rented by the gang in a wealthy Santiago suburb, Velasco said.

Carrillo, 42, died a day after returning to Mexico. According to Mexican officials, he was killed by a lethal dose of medicine after undergoing hours of plastic surgery in a desperate bid to change his appearance.

His nickname, "The Lord of the Skies," came from his use of passenger jets to transport tons of cocaine from South America to Mexico. He was chief of the Juarez cartel, based in a northern Mexico border town.
Although Chile has been spared the narco-violence suffered in other countries in the region, drug-trafficking and money laundering are on the rise.
Chilean police made their biggest-ever drug bust five months ago when they smashed a multi-million dollar ring smuggling cocaine from Peru and Bolivia through Brazil to Europe.
